question.problem: Find a unit normal vector to the level curve of the function $f(x,y)={x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-2xy+8y$ that passes through the point where $(x,y)=(2,-2).$
question.worked_solution:
A normal vector to the level curve that passes through the point where $(x,y)=(2,-2)$, can be found by computing $∇f(2,-2).$ 

So, we first find the gradient of $f(x,y)$ and evaluate it at $(x,y)=(2,-2):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-2xy+8y)\text{ }i+\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2}-2xy+8y)\text{ }j \\  & =(2x-2y)\text{ }i+(2y-2x+8)\text{ }j \\ ∇f(2,-2) & =(2(2)-2(-2))\text{ }i+(2(-2)-2(2)+8)\text{ }j \\  & =8\,i\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we normalize $∇f(2,-2):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∇f(2,-2)}{‖∇f(2,-2)‖} & =\frac{8\,i}{\sqrt{{8}^{2}}}=i\end{aligned}
$$
